client_brief:
Harborline Realty: Weekly listing sheet run: printer's book

Project overview
Harborline is a small owner run brokerage that lists the whole mid coast book, a three hundred and twenty thousand dollar starter one week and a waterfront estate the next. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Weekly listing sheet run: printer's book, per property files and the flagship proof and Eleven listing heroes brought to two tier targets.

What we will provide
listingsheet_2025_press.pdf; hero_selects/ (11 frames, 3600 to 4200 px long edge); weekly_active.csv; officesign_photo.jpg; principal_note.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Weekly listing sheet run: printer's book, per property files and the flagship proof: One page per genuinely active property, page count equal to the reconciled roster, each page binding address, headline, description, the beds and baths and square feet strip, price, agent and reference code verbatim plus that property's own hero photograph. 
- Eleven listing heroes brought to two tier targets: Eleven photographs from two sources and two times of day brought to two declared targets, one per tier, with one black point and one warmth and one crop logic inside each tier, and a stated reason for every difference between the tiers. 

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$1,400-$3,800 fixed; target delivery 7 to 15 business days; one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork posting quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, whose client was 'seeking a talented designer to create a real estate flyer for a new listing' that 'should be visually appealing and effectively communicate the property's features and benefits'. Laundered to the fictional Harborline Realty (principal Dana Marlow, listing agent Theo Vane); no real brokerage, agent, portal or trademark is named. The ledger conceded that the raw brief implies a from scratch flyer layout, which the connector cannot compose, and that the task as first carved sat on one surface. The fuller commission that brokerage actually has is the one it runs every Monday: the whole active book as a repeatable record per page run, rebuilt out of a press file left behind by a retired printer, fed by photography arriving from two sources at two price tiers, paired with an open house set the office must be able to change itself when a price moves.

The ledger conceded that the raw brief implies a from scratch flyer layout, which the connector cannot compose, and that the task as first carved sat on one surface. The fuller commission that brokerage actually has is the one it runs every Monday: the whole active book as a repeatable record per page run, rebuilt out of a press file left behind by a retired printer, fed by photography arriving from two sources at two price tiers, paired with an open house set the office must be able to change itself when a price moves.
price_band_and_audience: One brokerage, two audiences in one weekly run. The point estate at 4.5 million is bought by buyers over fifty with liquid capital who read restraint as credibility: one photograph, deep margins, quiet type, a price set small. The starter at 320 thousand is bought by first time buyers under thirty five who need price, beds and the open house time to land instantly: brighter, denser, price forward. The band is load bearing because a single blanket treatment fails in both directions at once. Style the whole book like the estate and the starter sheets look empty and evasive; style it like the starter and the estate reads as volume agency work in front of a vendor paying a six figure commission. A weekly production retainer of this shape posts at 700 to 1,600 dollars a month.

brand_identity.sector: Independent residential brokerage selling coastal Maine homes, from corner lot starters to waterfront point estates, to local and out of state buyers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2009, harbour front office on the mid coast of Maine, eight agents under principal Dana Marlow.
brand_identity.about: Harborline is a small owner run brokerage that lists the whole mid coast book, a three hundred and twenty thousand dollar starter one week and a waterfront estate the next. It runs on repeat referrals and reputation in town, and prints a fresh listing sheet for every active property each Monday. Dana Marlow built it to feel like the place it sells, not a national franchise.
brand_identity.audience: Two buyers in one weekly run: estate buyers over fifty with liquid capital who read restraint as credibility, and first time buyers under thirty five who need price, bed count and open house time to land at a glance.
brand_identity.price_positioning: One brokerage spanning a 320 thousand dollar starter to a 4.5 million dollar point estate; the sheet has to flex between the two without either register looking wrong. Weekly production retainer, roughly 700 to 1,600 dollars a month.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet transitional serif for headlines and prices, an even colour that reads calm on the estate sheets. A clean humanist sans for the beds, baths and square feet strip and the agent line. Estate sheets lean on space and small type; starter sheets carry weight and size so the price reaches across a room.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, grounded, mid coast. We describe the house, not ourselves, and never oversell. Example line the brand would write: 'Corner lot, three beds, a short walk to the harbour. Open Sunday, one to three.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original logo artwork was lost years ago. The only surviving version of the mark, a rope ring around a lighthouse with the letters H and R, is the one painted in cream on the office window. There are no brand guidelines or type specimen; the retired printer's last press file is the sole reference for the listing sheet.
brand_identity.values: Honesty about price and condition, and one consistent office look across every listing no matter who shot the photograph.

assets_supplied.name: listingsheet_2025_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The retired printer's flat press PDF of the office listing sheet, US Letter portrait, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries an address line, a headline, a three line description, a beds and baths and square feet strip, a price, an agent line, a small reference code line, and one placed hero photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The sheet our printer ran last year. It is the only file we have and she has retired."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither announced. What the conversion exposes as editable structure is a property of how she built the 2025 document: the description, the beds and baths strip, the price and the small reference code arrive inside ONE continuous flow while the address and the agent line sit alone, and the mapping readout silently omits the reference code run while keeping its line break, so every offset past it is short by that run's length and the validator still returns VALID. Separately the hero frame's real bounds are close to square rather than the letterbox the printed sheet suggests, and its fitting is a centre anchored proportional fill that is exposed in no readout at all, so the frame re crops whatever image is bound into it from its own centre regardless of how that image was prepared.

assets_supplied.name: hero_selects/ (11 frames, 3600 to 4200 px long edge)
assets_supplied.kind: One chosen hero photograph per active property, arriving from two sources: four shot by the brokerage's hired photographer for the expensive listings, seven shot by agents on phones.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One picture per house. Some ours, some the photographer's. They need to look like one office."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The two sources do not merely differ in quality, they differ in direction: the photographer's four are late afternoon, warm and deep with the interior lights carrying; the agents' seven are flat midday with a cold cast off the ocean and a lifted black point that reads clean alone and grey the moment it sits beside a photographer's frame. Two of the agent frames sit a degree or so off level and straightening them consumes exactly the edge margin any subsequent crop wants. One agent frame is a twilight exterior whose windows are clipped to paper white with no data behind them, so a highlight recovery there returns a file identical to the one it was given.

assets_supplied.name: weekly_active.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Monday export from the office system, one row per active property, with columns for address, headline, description, beds and baths and square feet, price, agent, reference code and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This week's eleven. Straight out of the system."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three faults, none stated. One property went under contract on Thursday and the office manager has not pulled it, so the export carries a row that must not print. The point estate's row was typed by the listing agent rather than exported, so its address uses a different abbreviation convention, its price carries a currency symbol the other rows do not, and its description runs roughly three times longer than anything in the 2025 book the sheet was built around. One photo cell names a file that does not match any folder name because the agent renamed the frame after exporting.

assets_supplied.name: officesign_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the brokerage's harbour front office window, the house mark painted on the glass in cream: a rope ring enclosing a lighthouse and the letters H and R.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "That window is the only place our mark still exists. We lost the artwork years ago."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark traces convincingly at the size the trace comes back, and the failure is entirely one of reproduction size: the rope ring is drawn as a repeating gap and twist, and the R carries a small enclosed counter, and neither of those is a property the trace controls. Vectorize takes no options whatsoever, so nothing about the trace can be tuned after the fact. Whether the gaps and the counter survive is decided by how many pixels the mark occupied in the raster that went in, and it can only be seen at the size the mark is actually used, on the ground it is actually used on.

assets_supplied.name: principal_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page from Dana Marlow on how the office wants to sit against the two other agencies in town, and what she means when she says a sheet looks cheap.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we want to look on the point and how we want to look in town."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the sheet's hero frame actually treats an image bound into it. The frame's bounds can be read out of the converted document, but its FITTING cannot: nothing in the conversion result, the mapping readout, the validator or the merge response says whether a bound image is fitted to the frame, filled from its centre, or placed at its own size. On this document it fills from the centre, so the subject aware crops prepared three steps earlier are re cropped again by the frame, and on the properties whose houses were composed off centre for good reasons the frame's centre lands on driveway and hedge and takes the roofline off the top. Every call in the chain reports success and the thumbnail of the prepared hero is still perfect.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. Reading bounds and preparing to that aspect is exactly what a careful agent does, and it does not help, because the frame re crops a correctly shaped image from its own centre. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for sheets that look like one office and never mentions frames or fitting, and the acceptance line about the whole house still showing is the client's standing requirement, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a changed crop policy for the whole set, decided against a fitting behaviour nobody could have known.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compare each rendered page's hero against the file that was bound, establish what the frame is doing to it, then return to the imaging surface and re derive the affected heroes with the house placed for the frame's centre rather than for the photograph, re read every tradeoff record so the re crop has not pushed anything into interpolation, rebuild the image map and merge again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A four and a half million dollar estate goes onto a vendor's sheet with its roofline sliced off and a hedge in the middle of the frame, and seven other sheets go out mis framed in the same silent way, while every file the agent prepared looks perfect on disk.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That one merged record does not fit and does not say so. The description frame was built by the retired printer at a fixed measure for a 2025 book whose entries were short. The point estate's description, typed by the listing agent rather than exported, is roughly three times that length. Overset text in a fixed frame does not spill and does not error: it simply stops rendering, so the page comes back looking finished with the description ending mid sentence at the trim edge. No tool reports overset anywhere in the chain, the merge returns success, and the page count is right.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot settle it: the frame's real capacity for a specific string at that document's point size and leading is not computable from anything the connector exposes, and there is no overset readout to query. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says prices went out wrong once and asks for a clean weekly run; no asset note, deliverable or earlier step mentions copy length. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is editorial: decide which facts a four and a half million dollar listing cannot lose and which are decoration, rewrite in the office's voice, and only then merge again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every rendered page at trim rather than at proof scale, identify each record that stops rather than ends, cut the offending copy to the measure the frame actually holds while keeping the estate's selling facts and the office's voice, raise the rewrite with the listing agent because it is his copy, then re normalise the data file and re run the merge and the per property branch.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The single most expensive listing in the book goes to every open house on a sheet whose description stops mid sentence, in front of the buyers the vendor's commission depends on, and the office's stated reason for hiring a designer was that the sheets keep going out wrong.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered house mark holds at the size it is actually used. The trace comes back at the size of the raster that went in, and at that size it is clean: the rope ring reads as rope, the R has a counter, the lighthouse has a door. Placed at the size a corner mark actually occupies on a square post and a tall story, and rendered on the cream ground the set uses rather than on white, the rope's gaps and the R's counter can close into solid shapes. Vectorize takes no options at all, so nothing about the trace can be tuned afterwards, and whether this particular mark survives is decided by how many pixels it occupied in the raster and by the ground it lands on.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it, because the judgement needs the mark at final size on the final ground, which exists only after the set is authored and exported. Care cannot settle it either: the trace looks correct at every scale before that one. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that the mark on the posts has to be the office's own mark rather than something close to it, which is a provenance requirement, not a warning that a trace can fill in. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The fix lives two surfaces back in raster preparation: re crop the window photograph so the mark occupies far more pixels, re select at ink level and trace again, which is new imaging work and a new judgement.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Inspect the exported canvases through the returned markup and the rendition rather than trusting the export, and where the mark has filled in, return to the window photograph, re crop tightly so the mark carries more pixels, re run the ink level selection and the trace, strip the background path and re inject a viewBox, then re author and re export the set and check the mark on the actual ground again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The office's only surviving mark goes out on public posts as a solid blob with no rope and no letterform, next to printed sheets carrying the real thing, which is the precise brand drift the principal hired a designer to stop.

decision_gates: Which deliverables go to the merge surface and which to authored canvases, given a sheet the office wants kept and prices that move on Thursdays.
How many targets the photography gets: one, which is safe and fails the brief in both directions, or two, which is the design answer the client described without naming.
Which tier each property belongs to, when the export carries no tier column and the boundary between them is a judgement about price, buyer and neighbourhood.
How much edge the two straightened agent frames can afford to give a crop, and whether the twilight exterior joins the set at all.
The roster: a property under contract that must not print, a hand typed estate row that matches nobody else's conventions, and a photo cell naming a file that does not exist.
Whether to trust the mapping tool's readout of the printer's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the exported document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template's placeholders.
Whether per property identity is established by position in a returned list or by opening the file.

The point estate proof is rendered at true print resolution at sheet trim, not at screen scale.
The book contains exactly one page per property that is genuinely active, no extra page and no missing page, and any row left out is named to us with the reason.
Every field the 2025 sheet carried is present on every page, including the small reference code, and nothing ends mid sentence at trim.
Every supplied asset is listed in the delivery manifest as used, reference-only, superseded, or rejected with a concrete reason; no input disappears silently.
Final files open successfully, use unambiguous names, match the stated dimensions and formats, and include editable sources only where the scoped deliverable requires them.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the folders into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome picture of a flyer. IDENTITY: these are eleven actual properties at actual addresses with actual prices, and the mark is the office's own painted mark, which has to be RECOVERED from the window rather than redrawn, because a brokerage cannot put an invented house or an approximated logo in front of a vendor. SPEC: the print shop needs one page per active property, page count equal to row count, every field bound verbatim including a reference code, plus one named file per property that actually contains that property and a proof at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the open house set is defined by being editable, because the price moves on Thursday and the office refuses to pay twice. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: what the frame does to a bound image, whether a record stopped rather than ended, whether a trace still reads at the size it is used.
